substitutions.from: A Leg carries no reader state (kogaki#1699): what a Leg's Move takes up and leaves is the Move's own `takes` and `leaves`, which `moves_you_may_bind` carries per Move, read as abstract constraints and never copied into the Leg. TAKE: every Leg binds a Move whose `takes` entries are each met by an entry an earlier Leg's Move leaves and no Leg between has taken up, or, on the first Leg, by what the Persona's prior-knowledge line supplies, which the assigned opening Move's `takes` already meet -- the kinds matching as words and the `what` lines by sense, never verbatim. LEAVE: every entry a Leg's Move leaves is taken up by a later Leg's Move, or is left by the Leg marked `reaches_target` as what the article leaves the reader with, and a `carry` is never left at the end.

substitutions.from: A reinforcing waypoint -- an example, a consequence, an answer to an objection -- names in `serves` the claim it reinforces; and a waypoint whose point no claim of the Leg supports is the signal to pull in a Journey, bind another Move, or report `no_move_fits`, never to write the waypoint anyway.
substitutions.to: THE STRUCTURE STANDS IN FOR STRANDS (kogaki#1664): Claim N is the `holds` sentence of entry N of `claims` in the input, addressed `L<N>` as its `claim_strand`, and its `proposition` is that sentence word for word; the Leg carries ONE Claim per entry, and Leg Waypoint N names in `serves` the Claim of entry N. Leg Waypoint N's `point` is written from entry N's `material`, the `context` of each Role and the `holds` of each relation the entry relates, and no `point` carries a word of `forbidden_words` in the input: the content words of the Strand's own claim, which the reader does not hold.

substitutions.from: How many waypoints a Leg carries is yours, and you need not reproduce the Move's internal structure element for element.

substitutions.from: THE RENDERINGS RECORD (kogaki#1494): `renderings` in the input lists the served words this article does not keep, each with the plain phrase it uses instead, and `strand_claims` carries each Strand's served claim; a claim's `proposition` and a waypoint's `point` use a served word as served or as its declared rendering, and no third form -- a word that is neither in the served claim of the Strand it draws on, nor a declared rendering of a word in it, nor in the `introduces` of its Leg or an earlier one, nor a function word, fails the Path Review naming the word; a served word with no entry is kept as served, and no `introduces` entry carries a term the record renders, which adoption refuses.
substitutions.to: THE WORDS ARE THE STRUCTURE'S (kogaki#1664): this Brief composes no renderings record; Claim N's `proposition` and Leg Waypoint N's `point` are written in the words of entry N's `material` -- a word that is in none of it and is not a function word is refused naming the word.

smp_leg_unit.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying `legs`, an array of EXACTLY ONE Leg, and nothing else. The Leg carries exactly these keys: `leg_id`; `purpose`; `rationale`; `claims` -- one `{ "type": "strand", "strand": "L<N>", "proposition": <entry N's holds, word for word> }` per entry of `claims` in the input, in order; and `waypoints` -- one `{ "point": <one sentence>, "serves": ["L<N>"] }` per entry, in order. It carries no `introduces`. Every field means what src/leg-schema.json, rendered below, says it means. The Harness writes `materials` and `depends_on`.
smp_leg_unit.refusal: a key the record or the Leg does not declare, or a declared key missing; an `introduces`; not exactly one Leg; a Claim whose `proposition` is not its entry's `holds`; a `point` carrying a word of `forbidden_words`, refused naming the word and the field; and the Proof Sheet's `validateLegPathUnit` over the Leg, imported, with each entry's `material` as the text its Claim and point are recovered from. Each refusal is put back into your next attempt verbatim.

sme_map_roles.note: The first Structure-Mapping Engine (kogaki#1665): one call reads the proposition into a RelationalStructure for the Persona. A second variant is a second row and a second Trial, never an edit of this one.
sme_map_roles.judgment_point: read the proposition in the input, `proposition`, as a relation among Roles. For each Role, name in one or two sentences, as its `context`, what a reader with the Persona in `persona` must come to hold, in the reader's own world, using no word of the proposition that is not a function word, and name, as its `attributes`, the one-place predicates the proposition states of that Role's object, each one short phrase in the proposition's own words, or an empty list where it states none. Name each relation among Roles as the proposition states it, as its `holds`, again using no content word of the proposition, with `between` naming the Roles it relates. Name the one relation among those relations the proposition turns on, as `higher_order`, with `relates` naming the relations it relates and `holds` stating it in the same words of the reader's world. Answer the RelationalStructure record and nothing else.
sme_map_roles.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `strand` -- the input's `strand`, verbatim; `roles` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id>, "context": <one or two sentences>, "attributes": [<one short phrase of the proposition>, ...] }`; `relations` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id, no Role's>, "between": [<two or more Role ids>], "holds": <one sentence> }`; and `higher_order` -- `{ "relates": [<two or more relation ids>], "holds": <one sentence> }`.
sme_map_roles.refusal: a key the record, a Role, a relation or `higher_order` does not declare, or a declared key missing; an id that is empty, repeated, or names nothing; a `strand` that is not the input's; a `context` or `holds` carrying a content word of `proposition`, refused naming the word and the field; and a Role without `attributes`, refused naming the Role, an `attributes` that is not a list, refused naming the Role, or an entry that is empty, not text or repeated within the Role, refused naming the Role and the index. The first refusal is put back into your next attempt verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial.

smp_bind_move.note: The short Trial's `bind` stage (kogaki#1700): one model call binds the Move of the Base Paragraph to the structure, and the Move of the Inference Paragraph where the base Move leaves a `carry`, before any base is named. Under the Mapper's one-retry bound.
smp_bind_move.judgment_point: choose ONE Move of `moves` in the input for the Base Paragraph: a Move whose `segments`, in order, can carry the relations and then the higher-order relation of `structure`, and every entry of whose `takes` the reader in `persona` meets from `persona.prior_knowledge`. Answer its id as `base_move`. Then read that Move's `leaves`: where it holds an entry of kind `carry`, choose ONE Move of `moves` for the Inference Paragraph whose `takes` holds an entry of kind `carry`, and answer its id as `inference_move`; where it holds none, answer `inference_move` null, for no Inference Paragraph is owed. Name in `rationale`, in one or two sentences, why the Segments of the base Move carry the structure. Choose no base domain and no wording: they are named after this call, under the Move you bind.
smp_bind_move.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `base_move` -- one Move id of `moves`; `inference_move` -- one Move id of `moves`, or null; and `rationale` -- one or two sentences.
smp_bind_move.refusal: a key the record does not declare, or a declared key missing; a `base_move` or `inference_move` naming no Move of `moves`, refused naming the id; an `inference_move` null where the base Move leaves a `carry`, refused naming the entry; an `inference_move` given where the base Move leaves no `carry`; an `inference_move` whose `takes` holds no `carry`, refused naming the Move; and a `rationale` that is not one non-empty text. The first refusal is put back into your next attempt verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `bind`.

smp_correspondence.note: The short Trial's `correspondence` stage (kogaki#1700): one model call fills the Correspondence column under the bound base Move's Segments. Its answer is validated by `validateRbsTable` as the owner's file is (kogaki#1693). Under the Mapper's one-retry bound.
smp_correspondence.judgment_point: name ONE domain the reader in `persona` already holds, from `persona.prior_knowledge`, in which the Roles, the relations and the higher-order relation of `structure` hold as stated and in which the `segments` in the input, the Segments of the Move bound to the Base Paragraph, can be performed in order. A Segment asking for an everyday case yields a domain apart from the proposition's; a Segment asking for a plain restatement yields the proposition's own. Name the domain in one phrase as `base.domain`. Then name, for EVERY Role of `structure`, in the structure's order, one Correspondence expression as its `expression`: a noun phrase of that domain naming the object that plays the Role, written so that it reads in place of `{<id>}` in each `holds` sentence, where `{<id>}` stands for the Role of that id. No expression uses a content word of the proposition: the reader does not hold the Strand's words.
smp_correspondence.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `base` -- `{ "domain": <one phrase> }`; and `correspondences` -- one `{ "role": <the Role's id>, "expression": <one noun phrase> }` per Role of `structure`, in the structure's order.
smp_correspondence.refusal: a key the record does not declare; a `base` that is not `{ domain }`, refused naming the key; an `expression` that is not one non-empty text, or that carries a content word of the proposition, refused naming the word and `correspondences[<i>].expression`; a `role` naming no Role of `structure`, refused naming the id; and a Role with other than one correspondence, refused naming the Role. The first refusal is put back into your next attempt verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `correspondence`.

smp_waypoints_unit.note: The short Trial's `waypoints` stage (kogaki#1700): one call writes the Paragraph Waypoints of the Base Paragraph and, where one is owed, the Inference Paragraph, with each Move already bound by `bind`.
